candidates.mechanism: Perpetual-futures funding pressure may contain incremental information about near-term panel return.
candidates.falsifiable_claim: Funding pressure adds information about the next 24h fixed-panel return beyond recent panel return.
candidates.conceptual_feature: Cross-sectional mean funding pressure observed at the completed decision boundary.
candidates.required_timing_semantics: funding known only after its published event timestamp; OHLCV safe-known-after bar close
candidates.why_incremental_information_could_exist: Funding transfers can encode positioning pressure not contained in price-only return history.
candidates.strongest_alternative_explanation: Funding is a proxy for the same price trend and volatility state already in the baseline.
candidates.strongest_falsifier: No incremental association after the fixed baseline and timing contract.
candidates.relation_to_existing_jigsaw_evidence: Structural extension of funding-pressure work; no funding field is in the RDS V0 OHLCV contract.
candidates.relation_to_v0_v1_candidates: Not a V1 finalist; V1 had no funding-pressure candidate.

candidates.mechanism: Panel breadth may convey cross-asset risk appetite relevant to BTCUSDT return.
candidates.falsifiable_claim: Fixed-panel breadth adds positive incremental information about BTCUSDT next 24h return beyond BTCUSDT recent return.
candidates.conceptual_feature: Mean sign of completed hourly returns across the fixed panel.
candidates.required_instrument_class: fixed panel plus BTCUSDT USD-M perpetual
candidates.required_timing_semantics: all features known after completed source-bar close; outcome starts next hour
candidates.why_incremental_information_could_exist: Breadth can summarize market-wide participation beyond focal-asset history.
candidates.strongest_alternative_explanation: Breadth is only a correlated transform of common market movement.
candidates.strongest_falsifier: No incremental association after BTC baseline.
candidates.relation_to_existing_jigsaw_evidence: Historical extension of JH03 breadth-to-return; no BTCUSDT is in RDS V0.

candidates.mechanism: Cross-sectional dispersion may precede elevated aggregate panel volatility.
candidates.falsifiable_claim: Current fixed-panel cross-sectional return dispersion adds positive incremental information about future panel RV24 beyond current panel RV24.
candidates.conceptual_feature: Cross-sectional standard deviation of completed hourly panel returns.
candidates.conceptual_outcome: Next 24h root-sum-square of equal-weight panel hourly returns.
candidates.required_timing_semantics: feature cutoff at completed panel bar close; outcome starts next hour
candidates.why_incremental_information_could_exist: Cross-asset disagreement can signal latent repricing and risk transfer before aggregate variance rises.
candidates.strongest_alternative_explanation: Dispersion is a noisy proxy for current aggregate volatility.
candidates.strongest_falsifier: No incremental association after current panel RV24.
candidates.relation_to_existing_jigsaw_evidence: JH02 dispersion-to-RV used a related but distinct context; this is a fixed-panel aggregate extension.

candidates.mechanism: Return concentration may identify fragile aggregate panel states before dispersion changes.
candidates.falsifiable_claim: Current fixed-panel return concentration adds positive incremental information about future panel dispersion beyond current panel dispersion.
candidates.conceptual_feature: Maximum absolute completed hourly panel return divided by the sum of absolute panel returns.
candidates.conceptual_outcome: Panel cross-sectional dispersion at the next 24h origin.
candidates.required_timing_semantics: feature cutoff at completed panel bar close; outcome begins at t+24h
candidates.why_incremental_information_could_exist: A move dominated by one instrument may indicate fragile breadth and subsequent cross-sectional repricing.
candidates.strongest_alternative_explanation: The ratio merely rescales aggregate volatility or is dominated by one noisy bar.
candidates.strongest_falsifier: No incremental association after current dispersion.
candidates.relation_to_existing_jigsaw_evidence: No prior exact proposition; uses the fixed-panel evidence lineage only.
candidates.relation_to_v0_v1_candidates: Descends conceptually from JFPV1_04 but retains the new outcome-blind contract.

candidates.mechanism: Cross-sectional sign agreement may distinguish synchronized risk repricing from idiosyncratic movement.
candidates.falsifiable_claim: Current sign agreement adds positive incremental information about future panel RV24 beyond current panel RV24.
candidates.conceptual_feature: Absolute mean sign of completed hourly panel returns.
candidates.required_timing_semantics: feature cutoff at completed panel bar close; outcome starts next hour
candidates.why_incremental_information_could_exist: Synchronized movement can indicate common-factor repricing rather than isolated dispersion.
candidates.strongest_alternative_explanation: Sign agreement duplicates breadth magnitude and adds no distinct information.
candidates.strongest_falsifier: No incremental association after current panel RV24.
candidates.relation_to_existing_jigsaw_evidence: Related to breadth but a distinct absolute-agreement mechanism.
candidates.relation_to_v0_v1_candidates: New mechanism using prior panel evidence without copying a V1 formula.

candidates.mechanism: Downside-dominated panel variance may signal asymmetric stress before aggregate panel volatility rises.
candidates.falsifiable_claim: The share of recent panel return variance from negative returns adds positive incremental information about future panel RV24 beyond current panel RV24.
candidates.conceptual_feature: Sum of negative-return squares divided by total panel-return squares over the prior 24 completed hours, with positive denominator.
candidates.required_timing_semantics: feature cutoff at completed panel bar close; outcome starts next hour
candidates.why_incremental_information_could_exist: Downside asymmetry may encode stress not captured by total recent variance.
candidates.strongest_alternative_explanation: The ratio is a noisy transform of volatility level and recent trend.
candidates.strongest_falsifier: No incremental association after current panel RV24.
candidates.relation_to_existing_jigsaw_evidence: A panel-level historical extension of downside-share reasoning; no exact prior panel proposition.
candidates.relation_to_v0_v1_candidates: Distinct from V1 BTC downside-share candidate; not a relabeling of BTC data.
